findings.claim: Wildcard routing can select a less-specific hostname because candidates are sorted only by path-prefix length.
findings.evidence: With api.acme.localhost at root and acme.localhost at /api, admin.api.acme.localhost/ reached API but /api and /api/users reached ROOT.
findings.layer: built proxy end-to-end hostname and path dispatch

findings.claim: Standalone dot segments are accepted into stored route identity but canonicalized out of request paths, creating unreachable routes.
findings.evidence: normalizePathPrefix('/api/.') produced '/api/.' while URL.pathname produced '/api/'; the registered alias returned 404 for /api/., /api/, and /api/x.
findings.layer: stored route identity versus WHATWG request-path substrate

findings.claim: An explicit root --path cannot override PORTLESS_PATH or config because normalized undefined is treated as absence.
findings.evidence: PORTLESS_PATH=/api with --path / printed and registered http://precedence.localhost:18165/api.

findings.claim: The documented path configuration contract is incomplete and disagrees with multi-app and alias behavior.
findings.evidence: PORTLESS_PATH is advertised without its multi-app exclusion; path precedence and package.json support are omitted in canonical passages; alias help omits the accepted flag.
